/-!
# Conjecture 5.42

by A. Yu. Ol'shanskiĭ

Does the free group of rank 2 have an infinite ascending chain of verbal subgroups
each being generated as a verbal subgroup by a single element?

For an element $w$ of a group $G$, the verbal subgroup of $G$ generated by $w$ is the
subgroup generated by all values $\varphi(w)$ of $w$ under the endomorphisms
$\varphi$ of $G$. It is the smallest fully invariant (i.e. endomorphism-closed) subgroup
of $G$ containing $w$; in particular it is normal. For $G = F_2$ these values are exactly
the values of the two-variable word $w$ in $F_2$, so this is the verbal subgroup $w(F_2)$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.docstring:
Does the free group of rank 2 have an infinite ascending chain of verbal subgroups
each being generated as a verbal subgroup by a single element?

That is, are there elements $w_0, w_1, w_2, \ldots$ of the free group $F_2$ of rank 2 whose
verbal subgroups form a strictly ascending chain $V(w_0) < V(w_1) < V(w_2) < \cdots$, where
$V(w)$ is the subgroup of $F_2$ generated by all values $\varphi(w)$ of $w$ under the
endomorphisms $\varphi$ of $F_2$? The chain is required to be strictly increasing, so that
it is genuinely infinite.

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question (Prop: ∃ a strictly ascending sequence V_1 < V_2 < ... of verbal subgroups of F_2, each V_i the verbal subgroup of F_2 defined by a single word w_i, i.e. generated by all values of w_i under all endomorphisms/substitutions); 'verbal subgroup generated by a single element' means the smallest fully-invariant (endomorphism-closed) normal subgroup containing that word, and 'ascending' should be read as strictly increasing so the chain is genuinely infinite.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates encode the same (correct) reading: ∃ w : ℕ → FreeGroup (Fin 2) whose verbal closures ⟨φ(w_n) : φ ∈ End(F₂)⟩ form a strictly increasing chain, with answer(True) = positive answer. c07 was chosen as the base because its bespoke `verbalSubgroup (w : G)` most directly matches 'generated as a verbal subgroup by a single element' of the group, and its API lemmas (`verbalSubgroup_le_iff`, `map_verbalSubgroup_le`, `verbalSubgroup_normal`) certify in Lean that the definition is exactly the smallest fully invariant (normal) subgroup containing w, as the decomposition notes require; it also includes a sanity test (verbal closure of a free generator is ⊤). Edits: added docstrings to undocumented lemmas, slightly expanded module/theorem docstrings. c08's sInf definition, c01/c05's inline closures, c02's def, c03/c06's word-based definitions are all equivalent on this statement but less direct or less well tested.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.42

by A. Yu. Ol'shanskiĭ

Does the free group of rank 2 have an infinite ascending chain of verbal subgroups
each being generated as a verbal subgroup by a single element?

For an element $w$ of a group $G$, the verbal subgroup of $G$ generated by $w$ is the
subgroup generated by all values $\varphi(w)$ of $w$ under the endomorphisms
$\varphi$ of $G$. It is the smallest fully invariant (i.e. endomorphism-closed) subgroup
of $G$ containing $w$; in particular it is normal. For $G = F_2$ these values are exactly
the values of the two-variable word $w$ in $F_2$, so this is the verbal subgroup $w(F_2)$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.42»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- The verbal subgroup of $G$ generated by the single element $w$: the subgroup generated by
all values $\varphi(w)$ of $w$ under endomorphisms $\varphi$ of $G$. -/
def verbalSubgroup (w : G) : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure (Set.range fun φ : G →* G => φ w)

/-- An element lies in the verbal subgroup it generates. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem self_mem_verbalSubgroup (w : G) : w ∈ verbalSubgroup w :=
  Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨MonoidHom.id G, rfl⟩

/-- The verbal subgroup generated by the identity is trivial. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_one : verbalSubgroup (1 : G) = ⊥ := by
  simp [verbalSubgroup]

/-- The verbal subgroup generated by `w` is fully invariant. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem map_verbalSubgroup_le (w : G) (ψ : G →* G) :
    (verbalSubgroup w).map ψ ≤ verbalSubgroup w := by
  rw [Subgroup.map_le_iff_le_comap, verbalSubgroup, Subgroup.closure_le]
  rintro _ ⟨φ, rfl⟩
  exact Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨ψ.comp φ, rfl⟩

/-- The verbal subgroup generated by `w` is the smallest fully invariant subgroup
containing `w`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_le_iff {w : G} {H : Subgroup G} (hH : ∀ ψ : G →* G, H.map ψ ≤ H) :
    verbalSubgroup w ≤ H ↔ w ∈ H := by
  refine ⟨fun h => h (self_mem_verbalSubgroup w), fun hw => ?_⟩
  rw [verbalSubgroup, Subgroup.closure_le]
  rintro _ ⟨φ, rfl⟩
  exact hH φ ⟨w, hw, rfl⟩

/-- The verbal subgroup generated by `w` is normal. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
instance verbalSubgroup_normal (w : G) : (verbalSubgroup w).Normal where
  conj_mem n hn g := map_verbalSubgroup_le w (MulAut.conj g).toMonoidHom ⟨n, hn, rfl⟩

/-- The verbal subgroup of the free group of rank 2 generated by a free generator is the whole
group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_of : verbalSubgroup (FreeGroup.of (0 : Fin 2)) = ⊤ :=
  eq_top_iff.2 fun g _ => Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨FreeGroup.lift fun _ => g, by simp⟩

/--
Does the free group of rank 2 have an infinite ascending chain of verbal subgroups
each being generated as a verbal subgroup by a single element?

That is, are there elements $w_0, w_1, w_2, \ldots$ of the free group $F_2$ of rank 2 whose
verbal subgroups form a strictly ascending chain $V(w_0) < V(w_1) < V(w_2) < \cdots$, where
$V(w)$ is the subgroup of $F_2$ generated by all values $\varphi(w)$ of $w$ under the
endomorphisms $\varphi$ of $F_2$? The chain is required to be strictly increasing, so that
it is genuinely infinite.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.42» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ w : ℕ → FreeGroup (Fin 2), StrictMono fun n => verbalSubgroup (w n) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.42»

items: 'Single element' is read as an element of the free group F₂ itself (a word in the two free generators), with the verbal subgroup it generates being ⟨φ(w) : φ ∈ End(F₂)⟩, as prescribed by the decomposition notes. An alternative reading would allow w to be a word in arbitrarily many variables (an element of F_∞) with values taken under all homomorphisms F_∞ → F₂; the two readings are not obviously equivalent, so a reviewer should confirm the chosen one.
'Ascending' is read as strictly ascending (StrictMono on an ℕ-indexed sequence), following the decomposition notes; a non-strict reading would make the question trivial.
The chain is indexed by ℕ (order type ω), the standard meaning of an infinite ascending chain.

Verbal subgroups of F₂ coincide with fully invariant subgroups of F₂ (every verbal subgroup is fully invariant, and a fully invariant H equals the verbal subgroup defined by the word set H), so 'the verbal subgroup generated by w' is unambiguous: it is the smallest fully invariant subgroup containing w, which the API lemma verbalSubgroup_le_iff certifies for the chosen definition.
The definition is stated for an arbitrary group G (with variable {G : Type*} [Group G]) and kept in the problem file inside the problem namespace, since it is used only by this problem.

reviewer_notes: Interpretation: 'generated as a verbal subgroup by a single element' is read as the verbal closure in F₂ of an element w ∈ F₂ (the smallest fully invariant subgroup of F₂ containing w), which equals the subgroup generated by all endomorphic images of w. This agrees with the decomposition table and with the phrase 'generated ... by an element' (as opposed to 'defined by a single law'). Several candidates (c04, c06, c07) flagged the alternative reading where the single word may involve more than two variables (w ∈ F_∞, V = w(F₂)); that reading is not provably equivalent in general but is not the natural reading of 'element', so it was not adopted — a human reviewer may wish to confirm. 'Infinite ascending chain' is encoded as an ℕ-indexed StrictMono sequence (equivalent to ∀ n, V n < V (n+1) used by c01/c02/c05). Definition kept in the problem file per STATEMENTS.md (problem-specific definition); a reviewer could move it to FormalConjecturesForMathlib if desired. Final file compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning.
